editions.text:
The station logged 284 feeder visits and 23 species, a quieter day than the previous week’s average of 312 visits. Regulars like the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal held their ground, with the Titmouse accounting for the majority of visual visits. The Eastern Towhee was detected 102 times. The Northern House Wren returned after a 17-day absence.

Mourning Doves, present each of the last seven days, were absent today. A woodpecker brick installed on the cage-feeder earlier in the week and a seed-feeder refill on September 30 coincide with the continued presence of the Downy, Northern Flicker, and Pileated, who were detected throughout the day.

Activity spanned from just before sunrise, when a Northern Cardinal was seen, until 32 minutes before sunset, when a Tufted Titmouse made the last visit. The Eastern Screech-Owl was heard briefly in the evening.
